coverageNote: Disk enumeration matched the expected 8 units / 45 files exactly: the domain directory itself (career-finance-business-index.md, career-finance-business-cx.md, 23.08-point-of-need-insurance.md, 23.09-career-sustainability-signals.md) plus seven sub-domain directories 23.01-23.07, each with one *-index.md, one *-cx.md and 3-5 leaf feature files. Every file was read in full through the 3a->3b->3c cycle; no sampling. Structural verification was run programmatically: 8/8 indexes carry a populated Role Matrix, 8/8 CX files carry a Cross-Cut Map and Rejected Pairs, 29/29 leaf features carry a Role Lens plus Behavior / Edge Cases / States / Deep Think / Decisions / Open Questions, and no folder has a single child. Dimension 6 (Competitive Positioning) is marked N/A on every unit: it belongs to meta/competitive-landscape.md, which is outside this domain. All other dimensions were scored. Two units (23.01 and 23.07) produced no surviving finding after the devil's-advocate pass and are scored clean; 23.07.01 in particular demonstrates the tree's own convention of re-pointing deferrals away from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5, which is the convention the reported dimension-7 findings are measured against.

findings.claim: The domain-level Role Matrix is a lossy rollup of the seven sub-domain Role Matrices, no rollup rule is stated anywhere, and in at least three rows the rolled-up access level contradicts the child matrices — in one case it contradicts the explanatory prose printed directly beneath it in the same file. An implementer wiring Operator access from the domain matrix builds a different permission set than one wiring it from the sub-domain matrices, in both directions (over-granting on 23.01 and 23.06, under-granting on 23.04).
findings.evidence: career-finance-business-index.md:79 — "| 23.06 Advances, Commission & Recoupment | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only | ❌ None |" — contradicted by career-finance-business-index.md:94 in the same file's reading note: "no royalties to recoup against and no catalogue (23.06 — `❌ None` on 4 of 5 children)", and by 23.06-advances-commission-recoupment/23.06-advances-commission-recoupment-index.md:28-32 which gives Operator `❌ None` on 23.06.01/.02/.03/.05 and `👁️ Read-only` only on 23.06.04. Same class at career-finance-business-index.md:77 — "| 23.04 Deal & Contract Vault | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only | ❌ None |" — versus 23.04-deal-contract-vault/23.04-deal-contract-vault-index.md:27 "| 23.04.01 Contract Vault & Document Store | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ❌ None |" and 23.04.01-contract-vault-document-store.md:18 "| Operator | Full | Lease, licences to operate, supplier and insurance contracts." And at career-finance-business-index.md:74 — "| 23.01 Income Aggregation & Financial Identity | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ✅ Full | ❌ None |" — versus 23.01-.../23.01-...-index.md:30-32 which reduces Operator to `⚙️ Config` on 23.01.03, `📊 Reports` on 23.01.04 and `❌ None` on 23.01.05. The prose at career-finance-business-index.md:90-91 asserts the matrix as fact rather than summary: "Operator drops off progressively. They are `✅ Full` where the need is genuinely shared (income, invoicing, insurance)".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the domain Role Matrix or the sub-domain Role Matrix is authoritative for Operator access, and — if the domain row is a rollup — what rule produces `👁️ Read-only` from a child set of {❌,❌,❌,👁️,❌} in one row and from {✅,👁️,⚙️,❌} in another.

findings.claim: 23.02.02's Happy Path — the only worked example of the feature's central deliverable, the deduction category vocabulary — instantiates a jurisdiction that the same file's own resolved open question puts out of v1 scope, and which the same file's Edge Cases would refuse. The two statements cannot both hold: v1 encodes US rules alone, yet the specified flow declares UK jurisdiction and enumerates a UK vocabulary. No US vocabulary appears anywhere in the unit, so the file's only concrete instance of what capture will offer is an instance the scope decision forbids.
findings.evidence: 23.02.02-deduction-categorization-jurisdiction-rules.md:27-29 — "1. Musician declares UK sole-trader jurisdiction. 2. Their capture surface offers a UK-shaped vocabulary: equipment, instruments, rehearsal, travel, subsistence, home-studio use, professional fees. 3. They categorize a £320 pedal as equipment" — against 23.02.02-deduction-categorization-jurisdiction-rules.md:83 (Q-01) "~~Which jurisdictions at launch~~ is **RESOLVED — the United States only** … so v1 encodes US musician/sole-trader rules alone", and 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-index.md:48 (Q-01) "**RESOLVED — the United States only.** The launch market is locked to one jurisdiction, so v1 encodes US sole-trader (Schedule C) rules and nothing else". The file's own Edge Case at 23.02.02:38 would reject the Happy Path's premise: "| Jurisdiction not supported | Must fail honestly — a generic category list dressed as a rule set is worse than nothing | Explicit \"not supported; export raw data instead\"".
findings.forcedInvention: The v1 (US) category vocabulary, apportionment rule set and capital threshold that capture will actually offer — the file enumerates only the superseded UK set.

findings.claim: An unresolved product-behaviour question in 23.02.04 — whether withholding and reclaim entitlement attach to a Band entity or to its individual members — is deferred to `/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening`, a stage the ideation tree elsewhere records as run and closed, and carries no owner. It is covered by none of the file's three Open Questions (Q-01 booking-time relief, Q-02 treaty pairs at launch, Q-03 WeJammin as withholding agent), so after that stage closed the item lost both its owner and its live target. The tree demonstrates the correct handling of exactly this case elsewhere, which is why the omission is a defect rather than a convention.
findings.evidence: 23.02.04-cross-border-withholding-reclaim.md:42 — "| Band entity performed, individuals taxed | Withholding and reclaim entitlement may sit differently for the entity and the members | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — genuinely complex and jurisdiction-dependent |". The stage is recorded closed at 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity/23.01.03-multi-currency-fx.md:88 — "**Re-pointed**: `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and closed" — and again at 23.01.05-income-to-work-linkage.md:86. The correct remediation pattern is demonstrated at 23.07-budgeting-project-tour-pl/23.07.01-budget-actuals-tracking.md:87 — "**Deferral target re-pointed** from the completed `/ideate-discover` Step 5 run to `/write-be-spec`".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a Band-entity foreign performance produces one entity-level withholding position or N member-level positions, and which identity owns the reclaim — with no owner or stage assigned to decide it.

findings.claim: 23.03.02's entire jurisdiction-specific compliance surface is VAT/GST-shaped, but the domain records that the sole launch jurisdiction has no VAT/GST. The feature's stated identity is that compliance fields are what make an invoice payable, and it derives those fields from 23.02.02's jurisdiction rules — which v1 scopes to US Schedule C. The result is that the one feature whose value proposition is jurisdictional compliance specifies no compliance content that exists in the jurisdiction it will ship into, and the deferral covering the gap points at a closed stage.
findings.evidence: 23.03.02-invoice-issuance-compliance.md:39 — "| User is VAT/GST registered mid-year | Treatment changes prospectively; historic invoices do not move |" — and 23.03.02:41 "| Reverse charge / cross-border B2B VAT | Jurisdiction-specific and genuinely hard | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — depends on 23.02.02's jurisdiction rules |" — and 23.03.02:63 (DT-03) "for a UK sole trader below the VAT threshold, invoice formalism genuinely is light-touch". Against 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness/23.02-expenses-tax-readiness-index.md:50 (Q-03) — "Scope-narrowed by **D-32** (US-only launch): **there is no US VAT/GST**, and state marketplace-facilitator sales tax is provider-handled and explicitly not built". The dependency is asserted at 23.03.02:69 — "Depends on **23.02.02 Deduction Categorization & Jurisdiction Rules** for tax identity and treatment".
findings.forcedInvention: Which tax identifiers and compliance fields a v1 (US) invoice must carry for an AP system and a tax authority to accept it — the file names only VAT/GST registration status, reverse charge and the VAT threshold, none of which exist in the launch jurisdiction.

findings.claim: 23.03.03 commits to a specific automatic behaviour on statutory late-payment interest in its Happy Path while its own Open Question treats assert-versus-offer as undecided, and its Behavior section uses the opposite word. Unlike the comparable case at 23.01.01 Q-01 — which explicitly names its interim default and says downstream is unblocked — Q-03 records no interim, so the Happy Path silently pre-empts a question the file says is open. Two implementers reading independently build different products: one auto-names the entitlement in the day-14 message on the user's behalf, one offers it as an opt-in.
findings.evidence: 23.03.03-payment-chasing-dunning-aging.md:30 (Happy Path step 4) — "Day 14: a firmer reminder naming the statutory interest entitlement." — against 23.03.03:90 (Q-03) "Statutory late-payment interest — asserted automatically where the law grants it, or offered? Asserting it is legally correct and commercially aggressive on behalf of a user who may not want it asserted in their name." — and against the file's own Behavior at 23.03.03:23 which uses the weaker framing: "with statutory late-payment interest **available** where the jurisdiction grants it". Contrast the correctly-handled pattern at 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity/23.01.01-income-event-ledger.md:105 — "**Interim default already specified and downstream is unblocked** — DT-06, the Role Lens (Fan) and States → Empty all fix it at *first income event*".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the outbound ladder message asserts the user's statutory interest entitlement by default, or whether assertion requires per-invoice or per-counterparty opt-in.

findings.claim: 23.04.03 gates the top rung of its escalation ladder on a surface question that the project's constraints file has since closed. The feature's own design premise is that silence is the one unacceptable outcome and that a single email for a date worth a catalogue is negligent, yet its highest escalation channel is conditioned on mobile 'existing' — a condition constraints.md now satisfies at v1 via installable-PWA web push. An implementer following 23.04.03 ships email as the terminal channel for the domain's highest-consequence notification; one following the locked constraint ships web push in v1.
findings.evidence: 23.04.03-option-reversion-obligation-alerts.md:28 — "Each scheduled point starts in-app, and if not acknowledged escalates to email, then to push (once mobile exists — `meta/constraints.md` open surface question)." Against meta/constraints.md:293 — "| Mobile (PWA) | PWA over the Astro web app | N/A | **v1**: web is installable as a PWA (home-screen, web push for gig alerts …)" and meta/constraints.md:298 "**Structural Classification remains `single-surface` for v1** (one Astro web app + PWA)". The same closure is already recorded inside this domain at 23.02-expenses-tax-readiness/23.02.01-expense-receipt-capture.md:86 — "**RESOLVED — yes: v1 is web + PWA; a native app is phase 2.** … the installable PWA (home-screen + web push)". The stakes are set by this feature's own text at 23.04.03:60 — "**Must fail loudly.** A silently broken alert scheduler is indistinguishable from having no dates" — and by 23.04-deal-contract-vault-cx.md:50 "A single email for a date worth a catalogue is negligent design."
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the reversion/option alert ladder has a push rung in v1, and therefore whether the escalation chain terminates at email — a decision the file defers to a condition that is already met.

findings.claim: Whether the extraction feature accepts and comprehends non-English contracts is deferred to `/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening` — a stage the tree records as closed — with no owner and no live Open Question covering it. The file's three Open Questions cover liability for a wrong extraction (Q-01), whether contract text leaves the platform boundary for a model call (Q-02), and whether a human legal-review path replaces extraction (Q-03); none reaches multi-language handling. The item is therefore untracked rather than deferred, and it interacts with a `security-first` constraint the file itself flags as hard.
findings.evidence: 23.04.02-key-term-extraction-deal-summary.md:44 — "| Multi-language contracts | Territory-dependent | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |" — an empty 'What User Sees' cell, unlike every other row in the table. The stage is recorded closed at 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity/23.01.03-multi-currency-fx.md:88 ("`/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and closed"). The unresolved behaviour matters because the file otherwise commits to honest degradation for every other unreadable input — 23.04.02:40 "| Document is a photo of a fax from 2009 | Extraction quality collapses | Says so; degrades to custody-only rather than pretending |" — leaving no equivalent rule for a language the extractor cannot read.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a non-English contract is refused, stored custody-only, or extracted with degraded confidence — and, given 23.04.02 D-01's calibration rule, what confidence signal a cross-language extraction reports.

findings.claim: 23.05.03's central privacy control is stated as a hard, enforced threshold but is never given a value, and no tracked question assigns one. The file makes the threshold load-bearing in both directions — it is the sole defence against re-identification, and it is what determines whether the feature ever renders anything at all, which the file says will be the normal state for a long time. 'Hard minimum cohort size' is a normative statement untestable as written: two implementers picking k=5 and k=50 build a feature that is respectively usable-and-leaky or safe-and-permanently-empty.
findings.evidence: 23.05.03-peer-cohort-benchmarking.md:80 (D-03) — "| D-03 | Hard minimum cohort size, enforced; show nothing below it | Small cohorts are named individuals |" — with the same unquantified phrasing at 23.05.03:23 ("Benchmarks are **aggregates with a minimum cohort size**, below which nothing is shown at all") and 23.05.03:37 ("Hard minimum cohort size, enforced. Show nothing rather than something. This is a privacy control, not a UX preference"). The consequence of getting it wrong is stated at 23.05-career-progression-benchmarking-cx.md:62 — "a 'cohort' of four session drummers in one city is four named people, and one of them can work out the other three's rates" — and the consequence of setting it high at 23.05.03:51 — "'Not enough comparable data' — and this will be the normal state for a long time". None of Q-01 (who sees benchmarks), Q-02 (boundary with 22 Analytics) or Q-03 (consent to aggregate) assigns the value.
findings.forcedInvention: The numeric minimum cohort size k, and whether it is a single global value or varies by cohort dimension.

findings.claim: Two unresolved product-behaviour items in this unit are deferred to `/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening`, a stage the tree records as closed, with no owner and no live Open Question covering either. The cohort-dimensionality item is the operational half of the very threshold D-03 declares enforced — how many splits before a cohort is too small — so its loss of tracking compounds finding #008 rather than duplicating it.
findings.evidence: 23.05.03-peer-cohort-benchmarking.md:43 — "| Rates differ by genre, city, client type, union status | A single benchmark is meaningless across those splits | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` — how many dimensions before the cohort is too small to show? |" — and 23.05.01-career-goals-roadmap-templates.md:42 — "| Band-level goals | The band's goals vs the member's are different objects (01) | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |". The stage is recorded closed at 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity/23.01.05-income-to-work-linkage.md:86 — "**Re-pointed**: `/ideate-discover` Step 5 has run and closed". Neither item appears in 23.05.03's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 nor in 23.05.01's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 (both of whose first two rows are struck through as resolved).
findings.forcedInvention: The cohort dimensionality policy (which of genre / city / client type / union status may be combined before the cohort falls below the minimum), and whether a Band entity can hold goals distinct from its members'.

findings.claim: The recorded MoSCoW cut of 23.06.01 rests on a model the feature had already excluded, leaving the referral variant's scope undetermined. 23.06 D-03 and 23.06.01 D-01 specify the feature as referral-only and explicitly reject first-party origination; the domain index then records the feature as `Won't` on the ground that first-party origination is a licensed activity. The cut therefore addresses a version of the feature that the spec does not describe, while the question of whether the specified (referral) version happens at all remains live and unanswered in two places. An implementer cannot determine whether advance underwriting is out of scope entirely or awaiting an owner decision.
findings.evidence: 23.06-advances-commission-recoupment-index.md:44 (D-03) — "| D-03 | WeJammin does not originate advances first-party | Lending is a licensed activity … The defensible model is **referral against verified income** (23.01.04), where the platform's unique asset is the underwriting data, not the money." — restated at 23.06.01-advance-underwriting-offers.md:78 "| D-01 | Referral, not origination |". Against career-finance-business-index.md:128 (Q-08) — "23.06.01 is `Won't` because 'First-party origination is a licensed activity requiring regulatory permission, capital adequacy and KYC/AML'". Meanwhile the live question is carried unresolved in two files: 23.06-advances-commission-recoupment-index.md:51 (Q-01) "**[OWNER]** Does WeJammin **broker** advances (referral, fee, no balance sheet) or stay out entirely? … D-03 settles *how* (referral, never origination) but not *whether* — that half is still the owner's." and 23.06.01-advance-underwriting-offers.md:87 (Q-01) "**[OWNER]** Does WeJammin broker at all (parent Q-01)?".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the referral-brokered advance feature is in scope. The dependency chain is real either way: 23.06.03's positions are created by it (CX-02), 23.06.04 DT-02 routes a late runway gap to it, and 23.01.04 is described as existing partly to underwrite it.

findings.claim: The overlapping-commission case in 23.06.02 — a band with a manager whose members also have their own managers, producing competing claims on the same income at two entity levels — is deferred to `/ideate-discover Step 5 deepening`, a stage the tree records as closed, with no owner and no live Open Question covering it. This is a netting-sequence question in the sub-domain whose own D-02 declares the order of operations to be its spine, and the sibling ordering question (competing recoupment positions) was correctly routed to `/create-prd-architecture` while this one was not.
findings.evidence: 23.06.02-commission-representation-deductions.md:44 — "| Band has a manager; members have their own | Overlapping commissions on the same income at different levels | `[PENDING — /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]` |" — an empty 'What User Sees' cell. The stage is recorded closed at 23.01-income-aggregation-financial-identity/23.01.03-multi-currency-fx.md:88. None of 23.06.02's Open Questions reaches it: Q-01 is struck through as resolved by D-02, Q-02 is commission routing, Q-03 is whether the manager is a user. The sibling case was routed correctly at 23.06.03-recoupment-netting-ledger.md:87 — "| Q-02 | Priority between competing positions when no contract specifies it … | Agent | `/create-prd-architecture` |" — and the stakes are set by 23.06-advances-commission-recoupment-index.md:43 (D-02) "**The order of operations is the sub-domain's spine**, not an implementation detail".
findings.forcedInvention: Whether a band-level commission and a member-level commission both apply to one band income event, in what order, and against which base — or whether the ambiguity holds the row under 23.06.02 D-02.
